title: Fund growth without ceding control
triggers: I need investors to scale but I don't want to give up control
I want to raise money without losing control of my company
I need funding but I don't want to give away equity
I don't want investors telling me what to do

premises.claim: Reaching the venture's goal needs outside money now, beyond what revenue, customers or partners can fund within the current runway.
For this venture, taking outside money means selling ownership.
For this venture, giving up ownership means giving up control.
The control the founder wants to keep is one thing, not several separate rights.

dichotomy: Take outside money and lose control, or keep control and grow more slowly.
reframe: Which ways of funding {goal} keep the specific control rights the founder will not give up, in the {phase} phase?

look_for: funding structures that separate money from ownership
structures that separate ownership from votes, board seats or vetoes

reasoning: Restate the goal and the decisions hidden in the founder's sentence before proposing anything.
Test each premise as a yes/no proposition against the venture's facts; say unknown when the facts do not settle it.
Say whether the trade is false, a real trade-off, or a sequence.
Draw funding options only from a dated, cited lookup, never from memory.
Return decisions with open options. Do not pick one.

emits.question: Which control rights will the founder not give up?
options: vetoes over a sale or new money
day-to-day authority to run the venture

emits.question: Which way of funding the goal keeps the control rights the founder will not give up?

facts.control_rights: day-to-day authority and the timing of a sale

facts.goal: ship 500 units of a medical device through regulatory approval by 2028
facts.control_rights: a majority of the board and votes on every major decision
